candidate_privileged_fields.rationale: role appears in PATCH response as read-only value 'member'; not included in request body — server-assigned. Elevation to 'admin' would grant administrative access.
candidate_privileged_fields.expected_blocked_signal: 400 with error 'unknown_field' or 'role' field stripped from response (returned as 'member' unchanged)
candidate_privileged_fields.proof_of_success: Response body or subsequent GET /api/v1/users/me contains role:admin

candidate_privileged_fields.rationale: plan appears in response as 'free'; not sent in request. Assigning 'enterprise' would bypass payment for premium tier.
candidate_privileged_fields.expected_blocked_signal: 400 with validation error or plan remains 'free' in subsequent GET
candidate_privileged_fields.proof_of_success: Subsequent GET /api/v1/users/me returns plan:enterprise, or subscription API shows enterprise features unlocked

candidate_privileged_fields.rationale: email_verified is a boolean in response. Many apps gate email-change flows or sensitive actions behind this flag; forcing true for a newly-registered or changed email bypasses the verification step.
candidate_privileged_fields.expected_blocked_signal: Field is ignored — value remains unchanged on subsequent GET, or 422 unknown field
candidate_privileged_fields.proof_of_success: GET /api/v1/users/me returns email_verified:true for a freshly-created account that never confirmed its email

candidate_privileged_fields.rationale: Common Rails boolean column not in current response but frequently present in User model alongside role. If strong_params is misconfigured, it may be assignable even if omitted from API responses.
candidate_privileged_fields.expected_blocked_signal: 400 or field silently ignored; admin panel /admin still returns 403
candidate_privileged_fields.proof_of_success: GET /admin or /api/v1/admin returns 200; or response body contains is_admin:true after PATCH

candidate_privileged_fields.rationale: id is returned in response. Attempting to reassign own id to another user's id could cause account takeover or privilege confusion in apps without strict write-protection on primary keys.
candidate_privileged_fields.expected_blocked_signal: 400 'id is not permitted' or id unchanged in response
candidate_privileged_fields.proof_of_success: Response returns id:1 and subsequent GET /api/v1/users/me returns data for user 1 (admin or another account)

framework_hints: Rails (Phusion Passenger in X-Powered-By header): strong_params bypass risk — if the controller uses .permit! or the params hash is passed to update() without explicit whitelisting, any top-level User model attribute is assignable
api_versions: /api/v2/users/:id — admin read endpoint observed in JS bundle; test whether PATCH /api/v2/users/me exists and applies a different or absent strong_params filter
stop_conditions: GET /api/v1/users/me returns role:admin after the PATCH — this is sufficient proof of privilege escalation via mass assignment
GET /api/v1/users/me returns plan:enterprise after PATCH with plan:enterprise — sufficient proof of plan bypass
summary: PATCH /api/v1/users/me may accept role, plan, or email_verified fields via Rails mass assignment; highest impact is role:admin elevation granting full administrative access
